chapters.title: The charity's website and its hosting history
The WP2Shell hack: two CVEs chained together
Investigation concludes: the patch already held

key_ideas.text: The charity's WordPress site was compromised through "WP2Shell", an exploit chaining two 2026 CVEs together; the same technique hit hundreds or thousands of sites worldwide, not just this one.

Rather than blindly follow the host's suggestion to roll the site back a week and a half, Lee checked with the charity first, since a lot of real data had been entered ahead of a big event, then investigated instead.

The investigation method: an offline database export plus an SSH tar of the file tree, checked with an LLM coding tool, then verified core WordPress files against their checksums, matched every user account, and reviewed site options and content for hidden payloads.

Two suspicious file-manager scripts turned out to be Lee's own leftover admin tools from a prior migration, restored by the site's own backup and never actually exploited — a reminder to verify before assuming the worst.

The investigation concluded the mitigation patch was already applied and nothing malicious persisted, so the rollback and its week and a half of lost data were not necessary; Lee still rotated the admin passwords as a precaution.
